name: Ashwini Container Movers Limited
summary: The expanded truck fleet and port contracts create operating opportunity, but the qualified land-rights audit, unreconciled proceeds presentation and cash conversion prevent a reliable investment conclusion. Existing-fleet cash scenarios require faster collections or new financing to meet term maturities and maintenance. Hypothetical funded returns are diagnostics only; no IAS or favorable ranking is issued.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Financial-reliability hold, not a favorable recommendation. The fleet and port-terminal opportunity are real operating leads, but the audit exception and cash/financing evidence are unresolved. Diagnostic BQS 4.20, GQS 5.30, IAS NS; none ranks. Existing-fleet scenarios include all legacy claims and maintenance, rather than assuming IPO proceeds remain. The base cash path is unfunded and therefore has no shareholder IRR. A hypothetical 20 crore facility plus discounted equity produces 5.90%, not an available investment return. [S1–S5]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Cutoff 20 October 2026; last observed NSE session 19 October, with 20 October a market holiday. ASHWINI/INE1A6Q01010 has 15 million issued shares and eligible SM market. ₹162.10 is an end-of-day observation, not an executable bid. G1 Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Fail under the defined no-rescue stress, G4 Conditional. The integrity gate is not automatically failed by a qualified audit or time-constraint resignation. Confidence in existence of signed disclosures is distinct from confidence in asset rights, recovery timing and forecasts. [S1,U1,U2,M1,M_SECURITY_SPEC]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: The 13 canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 7, DUR 5, CAP 4, CASH 3, BAL 2, EXEC 4, EARN 4, R NS, D 1, P 4, L 2. Exact weighted arithmetic and missing-data bounds appear in the audit; no neutral replacement or reweighting. Revenue uses the prespecified 3 year comparison (18.89%), not a selected bullish window. No historical score 9–10 is assigned. A single severe cash-conversion year does not prove persistent capital destruction, so the optional GQS cap is not fabricated. G2 independently blocks IAS and all rankings; G3 would cap a numeric IAS at 3. [S1,S2]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: Ashwini owns trucks/trailers for container road logistics tied to JNPA and Hazira, with freight charges driven by completed movements, route lengths, cargo type and rates. The owned-fleet model provides service control but makes depreciation, replacement vehicles, driver availability, tolls and fuel central to owner earnings. Normalized annual depreciation ramps to 15.7 crore, anchored to gross vehicle assets 130.4724 crore over the disclosed 8 year life with an assumed 5% residual, rather than freezing the half-year-weighted FY26 charge. Maintenance at 1.15 times that charge approaches 18.055 crore. The presentation reports 401 vehicles at FY26 end, versus 266 in its FY25 chart; an August press release says 261. The model uses 266 explicitly and does not conceal the difference. Vehicle counts are management statements, not independent utilization audits. The March 2026 share note shows two principal holders at 32.40% each and reports no pledged shares at that date; later ownership/pledge changes are not inferred from that dated statement. September/December 2024 bonus issues make the presentation’s old unadjustedEPS incomparable with current per-share earnings. [S1,S4,S5]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Reliability, route density, specialized vehicles and recurring port relationships may improve repeat business, but no verified exclusive concession or durable pricing power is shown. Prospectus top 10 customer concentration fell from 69.88% in FY23 to 45.48% in FY25 and 35.25% inH1 FY26; top 1 fell from 20.89% to 11.60% and 7.36%. This diversifies customer exposure but does not remove common EXIM-cycle dependence. Contract duration is not automatically a minimum-volume guarantee. Logistics industry growth and peers cannot justify transplanting an asset-light multiple onto this financed owned-fleet model. [S2,S4,S5]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Primary operating revenue is ₹76.8708,78.7725,94.1205 and 129.188 crore across FY23–26, a 3 year CAGR 18.89%; annual additions are 1.9017,15.3480 and 35.0675 crore. No 5 year CAGR is available from six audited annual observations. FY26 growth 37.26% exceeds PAT growth 22.08%. Management reports 28,243 containers versus 25,201, up 12.07%, and average rate 38,086 versus 37,348, up 1.98%; their product grows about 14.29%, not 37.26%. The operating metrics therefore do not fully reconcile revenue, possibly because of mix/additional services; they are not treated as an audited volume-price bridge. The signed result table shows H2 FY26 revenue 74.2819 crore versus 48.5050 crore, up 53.14%, butPAT4.1544 crore versus 6.0555 crore, down 31.39%. H2 operating margin is 12.41%, versus 16.53% a year earlier and 27.0% inH1 FY26. H2 is the disclosed balancing period; noFY27 interim has been invented. [S1,S2,S4,S9]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The 401-truck installed fleet permits a utilization ramp without assuming a new acquisition. The model starts at the H2 FY26 annualized run rate and 12.41% operating margin, then ramps toward fleet productivity and price assumptions; base 18% and bull 21% margins explicitly require recovery, while funding replacement maintenance and working capital. The August presentation cites a ₹60 crore four-year terminal contract; the later release cites ₹35 crore over five years with 15 trailers initially. Customer-signed conditions and overlap are unknown, so neither aggregate is simply added twice to capacity-driven sales. The combined 22 crore annualized sensitivity actually worsens early funding because receivables must be financed. Announced revenue is not free cash or a funded growth runway. [S4,S5]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The June 30, 2026 signed audit is qualified because the auditor lacked sufficient evidence of ownership, lease, licence or other legal/economic rights supporting ₹3.6683 crore compound-wall and infrastructure CWIP. Management says the land is rented under a valid arrangement and that supporting documents are being provided. Construction contracts, an architect certificate and photographs did not resolve the auditor’s asset-recognition question. No subsequent substantive auditor clearance was located by the cutoff. The model gives the CWIP no separate recovery, but an analytical haircut is not a substitute for documentary remediation. This is not a finding of fraud, land loss or fabricated construction. The August 14 auditor resignation expressly cites preoccupation and time constraints and says it was not caused by concerns about the company, management, financial statements or audit. The audit committee accepted that explanation on August 29. Its statement that no deliverables remained outstanding addresses the resignation process, not resolution of the earlier CWIP qualification. The board appointed M R Naidu & Associates to the casual vacancy, and the September 28 AGM proceedings include appointment resolutions; final voting confirmation was not separately checked. Related-party schedules show ₹0.1549 crore BGS hire-charge entries in both creditor/debtor presentations with zero closing balances; they are not summed into an invented 0.3098 crore net cash transfer. Disclosed related-person/KMP payroll totals 0.7354 crore. Those relationships warrant arm’s-length review, not an accusation of diversion. [S1,U1,U2,S7,S8]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: The IPO monitor reports all ₹71 crore utilized, including ₹42.50 crore debt repayment, ₹9.03 crore truck purchases, ₹9.17 crore general corporate use and ₹10.30 crore issue expenses. It notes ₹0.18 crore shifted from general purposes to issue costs without an overall proceeds deviation. The annual cash-flow statement instead labels ₹13.4456 crore as issue expense and presents ₹12.7935 crore long-borrowing inflow, ₹3.0205 crore long-borrowing repayment and ₹1.7475 crore short-borrowing net outflow. These debt figures reconcile the ₹8.0255 crore increase in booked debt, and the full cash-flow statement reconciles the ₹0.4937 crore cash increase. Gross versus net debt presentation and tax/timing/classification may explain part of the difference, but a full reconciliation of the monitor’s gross repayment and ₹3.1456 crore issue-cost difference was not found. Neither difference is treated as proof of missing proceeds, diversion or an actual default. FY26 CFO is −₹0.841 crore before financing interest; after ₹6.5538 crore cash interest it is −₹7.3948 crore. Subtracting ₹54.5948 crore PPE and ₹3.6683 crore CWIP gives −₹65.6579 crore cash after interest and gross capex, before disposals/financing. A limited economic reclassification moves the 2.0224 crore fall in capital creditors out of CFO and into cash PPE purchases (56.6172 crore instead of 54.5948), leaving that total unchanged. CFO also includes a 0.0639 crore current FD purchase and 1.0459 crore recovery of long advances; it is not a clean recurring operating measure. More-than-six-month receivables grew from ₹3.8997 crore to ₹13.8992 crore,34.03% of net receivables;₹1.5945 crore is older than one year. The ₹0.8113 crore doubtful-debt charge is not subtracted again from net opening AR. Current tax ₹1.1410 crore and MSME interest ₹0.0209 crore are separate claims;₹1.1938 crore capital creditors are not ordinary supplier funding. Incremental NOPAT/capital proxy is 6.77%, versus assumed 12–15% hurdle, but late fleet purchases make a matured-cohort inference unsafe. [S1–S3]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: ₹162.10×1.5 crore issued shares gives ₹243.15 crore market capitalization. FY26 PAT/current shares is ₹9.3737, not the reported ₹12.32 weighted-average EPS. The balance-sheet bridge adds ₹70.6001 crore debt and subtracts ₹1.3924 crore cash before separate FD treatment. Ordinary bear/base/bull paths are unfunded, so terminal outputs are diagnostics with no IRR. Explicit hypothetical debt/equity branches return -20.48%/5.90%/21.76%, including 12% interest,5% equity fees and issuance at 50% of the reference price. The funded base requires about 14.97× exit operating EBIT rather than 10× to clear 15%; its conditional hurdle entry is ₹107.35. These are financing-dependent illustrations, not fair-value targets. [S1–S5,M1]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Even with no discretionary fleet additions and maintenance 1× depreciation, the restrained existing-fleet case with 16% terminal EBIT margin (above latest H2’s 12.41%),115-day collections and 10% loss on older AR reaches a ₹12.9460 crore funding gap. This supports a research G3 Fail, not a statement of actual insolvency: the post-March bridge is unreported and actual amortization/credit access may differ. Deferring first-year principal to month 12 does not fund the ordinary base. Even crediting the entire 6.6171 crore government asset immediately and delaying current principal to month 12, the restrained case still reaches a ₹6.9406 crore shortfall; this deliberately optimistic credit-access check is not an asserted tax refund. A countercase with 70-day collections,0.9× maintenance and month 12 current-principal settlement survives and returns 9.85%; it requires evidence before becoming the base. The model excludes speculative recoveries on CWIP and unsecured advances, and retains rather than erases tax/benefit/contingent claims. [S1–S3]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: 5× and 10× prices require 37.97% and 58.49% annual five-year appreciation without dividends, before dilution. Even the hypothetical funded bull is conditional on new financing and strong operating assumptions, not a demonstrated 37.97% annual compounding path. To multiply owner value, fleet utilization and collected operating earnings must outrun replacement capex, receivables and financing dilution for years. A 60 crore or 35 crore multi-year contract is cumulative revenue, not annual profit or incremental equity value. The evidence does not establish a 5× / 10× compounder. [S1,S4,S5]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Require the actual lease/licence documents and auditor response; bridge IPO bank uses, gross debt repayments and issue costs; obtain a current debt maturity/renewal schedule and recoverability of government/unclassified advances; track overdue debtors and fleet-level cash after maintenance. At ₹5 lakh illustrative size, observed-only 5% participation is 9.39 days, while conditional zero-filling is 11.44 days over 60 sessions. Four of 60 rows are missing, not proved zero trades. Three 1,000 share lots cost ₹486,300; four cost ₹648,400. REG1 low-PAN and irregular-SME-trading cautions apply 21 October, not retroactively 19 October. Verify spreads, circuits and depth at implementation. These are research triggers, not an automatic monitoring promise. [M1,M_REG1,M_REG1_FORMAT,M_SECURITY_SPEC]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: The company disclosed a revised ₹1.77 lakh including GST fine for delayed FY26 results and reports paying it in July 2026. It attributed the delay to audit completion and pending clarifications. A separate ₹11,800 including GST prior-intimation fine was challenged on the basis that June 30 was an adjourned continuation of the June 24 meeting; the September 2 filing says that waiver request was pending and admits late submission of the board’s comments. These are disclosed compliance matters, not a finding of intentional concealment. The model includes the known July payment, conservatively budgets the notice’s ₹11,800 waiver-processing fee in July, and retains the disputed ₹11,800 fine rather than assuming cancellation. The fee payment itself was not separately verified. The FY26 notes disclose an income-tax appeal of ₹0.4955 crore and a service-tax appeal of ₹0.5409 crore. They are contingent disputed amounts, not established payment orders or findings of tax evasion. The model pays half in year 2 and retains half at exit, with a full-payment sensitivity. Current status beyond the annual disclosure was not verified. Final classification remains a financial-reliability hold. Growth may create value if contracts turn into collected, maintenance-adjusted earnings, but no ranking or favorable investment label overrides unresolved G2 and no-rescue funding stress. A clear contract/asset-rights and cash reconciliation, evidenced refinancing or sustained faster collections would change the analysis; a replacement auditor appointment alone would not. [S1,S6]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: All figures are crore unless otherwise labeled. Signed annual and prospectus scopes, issuer operating statements, observed exchange data, calculations and assumptions are separated. The prospectus’s FY25 PAT 11.4524/CFO 19.9179 differ from the later comparative 11.5171/18.529; the PAT difference 0.0647 is arithmetically explained by 0.0385 higher employee expense and 0.0262 higher deferred tax in the prospectus. The restated signed equity 20.8429 also differs from its summary 20.4227 and later 21.8716. These are preserved as unresolved presentation/comparability questions, not summed or called missing cash. Every opening liability/credit receives one economic treatment. Restricted/unverified FD accessibility is not operational funding; unknown government balances are not automatic tax offsets. Model outputs depend on assumed dated collections/principal and cannot certify actual default, audit remediation, future funding or executable returns. [S1–S8,U1,U2]

GOV.reason: Specific unresolved qualification and delayed compliance reduce confidence; stated resignation reason and disclosed responses retained. No fraud inference or automatic severe-integrity override.

MOAT.reason: Route density and owned specialized trucks support service, but no proved pricing power or exclusive customer lock-in. Capital ownership alone is not a moat.

REV.reason: Chosen 3 year revenue CAGR 18.8923% across FY23–26 starts 7 in 15–20% band. No extra trajectory point from one strong year; four observations, not a 5 year CAGR.

DUR.reason: Port contracts and broader customer base add visibility, but exact minimum volumes, escalation, termination and contract overlap remain unknown.

CAP.reason: Incremental NOPAT/capital proxy is below a 12–15% cost-of-capital assumption, but late fleet purchases distort maturity. Mixed rather than proven persistently destructive cohorts; no growth override applied.

CASH.reason: FY26 negative pre-interest CFO, increased six-month receivables and unexplained OCA reduce cash realization. Older years had positive CFO; do not automatically call the latest build persistent or cap GQS without evidence.

BAL.reason: Cash 1.3924 against currentterm 18.282 and substantial totaldebt; no leftover IPO reserve. Funded resilience depends on collections/refinancing.

EXEC.reason: Fleet expansion and contracts are tangible, but capital intensity, cash collection and audit/compliance follow-through lag the growth narrative.

EARN.reason: H2 FY26 revenue rose 53.14% butPAT fell 31.39% year on year; operating margin 12.41% versus 16.53% a year earlier. Annual growth masks late-period deterioration. Tax, depreciation andotherincome require normalization; clean per-share compounding is unproved.

R.reason: NS: ordinary bear/base/bull cash paths are unfunded under stated claims/timing. A hypothetical funded case cannot supply an investable expected-return score; G2 hold independently blocks IAS.

D.reason: Severe funding and permanent-loss pathway under restrained existing-fleet stress. A favorable collection/maintenance countercase is disclosed, not ignored.

P.reason: Conditional funded base requires a materially higher exitmultiple to clear 15%, plus new financing. Reference price does not provide a wide error margin.

L.reason: Observed-only 5% exit 9.39 days starts 5; conservative conditional-zero-fill 11.44 days starts 3, reduced 1 point for lot granularity and weak observed market quality. Missing rows are not asserted zero trades.

valuation.horizon: October 31, 2026 scenario boundary to October 31,2031; dated October 19 quote used as reference. Equal five model years, not exact trade-date XIRR.
valuation.method: 67 monthly rows bridge March audited opening to October 2026 reference and five-year October 2031 exit. No reported FY27 interim is invented. 401 existing vehicles ramp from latest H2 FY26 annualized revenue and 12.41% operating margin toward FY26 average-fleet productivity assumptions; H2 is the issuer-disclosed full-year-minus-first-half balancing period, not a reportedFY27 interim; operating price/productivity are assumptions, not fleet additions. Contract announcements are not added to ordinary sales on top of fleet productivity. Annual depreciation approaches 15.7 crore, anchored to 130.4724 crore gross vehicle assets with 8 year life and 5% residual (15.4936 crore), plus otherassets; assumptions rather than issuer guidance. Maintenance 1.15 x depreciation; optional growth canceled. Current 18.282 crore term principal amortizes within 12 months, remaining 51.6412 over 48 months; exact contractual timing unresolved and month 12 current-principal alternative supplied. Existing drawn demand debt retained with interest and terminal subtraction, no undrawn facility assumed. Earmarked IPO cash is zero because monitor says fully used. Unknown government credits receive no net current-tax offset; unclassified operating assets are held as a floor, not automatically liquidated in stress. Opening capital-creditor, tax, MSME interest, fines and appeals are separate dated obligations. DTL/gratuity/deposit liabilities retained if unpaid. Long FD presumed restricted given collateral language, only terminal face value. CWIP and unsecured loan/long security/investment recoveries excluded conservatively, never a second EV asset. Hypothetical 20 crore new-debt plus discounted-equity branches carry interest,5% fees and dilution but are not committed financing or G3 evidence. Unfunded scenarios have no shareholder IRR.
